h1: The 7 Best Single Monitor Arms for Every Desk and Screen Weight, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Single Monitor Arms 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 single monitor arms compared on weight rating, reach, VESA fit, desk thickness and warranty, from under $25 up.
summary: WALI is the best single arm for most people, with a 26.4 lb flat-screen rating and 19.3 inches of reach. Suptek stretches further at 21.65 inches, VIVO is the pick for ultrawides up to 38 inches, and Amazon Basics is the only one with a stated warranty. ErGear is the sub-$25 starter.
intro: A monitor arm rarely fails on day one. It fails at month six, when the screen creeps down and you start nudging it back up. The usual cause is buying on screen size instead of weight and reach, because the spec sheets that matter hide behind the headline inch count. A cantilever arm only holds what its spring can balance.

We ranked seven single arms from listing data, comparing load rating, extension, height, tilt, VESA fit and desk-thickness limits. Weight is the first filter, because an arm is only as good as the margin between your monitor and its limit, and the desk edge is the second, since a clamp that does not fit makes every other spec moot.

products.name: WALI Single Monitor Arm
products.verdict: The highest weight rating in the group, with 19.3 inches of reach and full rotation.
products.description:
WALI's single arm takes flat screens up to 26.4 lb and curved ones up to 19.8 lb, across 13 to 34 inch panels on 75x75 or 100x100mm VESA. Reach is 19.3 inches, lift is 17.3 inches, and the head swivels 180 degrees each way and rotates a full 360.

It leads because it is the only arm here that tells you the flat-versus-curved weight split, which is how a careful maker rates a cantilever: a curved screen puts its weight further from the pole. Suptek reaches a bit further but WALI carries more, and that load margin is what stops long-term droop.

Buy it for a 27 to 32 inch monitor on a wood desk. Note that it is C-clamp or grommet only, and WALI itself recommends wood desks with no crossbeam under the top, so glass and thin-edge desks need a different arm.
products.idealFor: Owners of 27 to 32 inch screens who want maximum load headroom.
products.skipIf: Your desk is glass or has a crossbeam under the top.

products.name: Suptek Single Monitor Arm
products.verdict: 21.65 inches of extension and 18.7 inches of lift lead the field at a bargain price.
products.description:
Suptek's arm covers 17 to 35 inch screens with a 24.25 lb rating, 75x75 and 100x100mm VESA, tilt of plus or minus 80 degrees and a full 360 degree screen rotation. Extension hits 21.65 inches and height 18.7 inches.

That is the most reach on the list, which is why it edges VIVO for second. If your desk is deep or you sit back from a large display, the extra two or three inches beyond the others decide comfort. It also takes the thickest desks, up to 3.85 inches, with a tool-free clamp.

It is the pick for tall users and big desks. The catch is that long arms amplify any wobble: the weight-balanced mechanism is described as silent, but a lighter 24 inch display will ride higher than one near the 24.25 lb limit, so tune the tension carefully.
cons: Long arm leans on a sturdy desk
products.idealFor: Deep desks and tall users who sit well back from the screen.
products.skipIf: Your monitor is a lightweight panel under 10 lb.

products.name: VIVO Single Monitor Desk Mount
products.verdict: The only arm here that explicitly covers ultrawides up to 38 inches at 22 lb.
products.description:
VIVO's single mount holds up to 22 lb on 75x75 or 100x100mm VESA, covering 13 to 32 inch monitors and ultrawides up to 38 inches. Tilt runs plus or minus 90 degrees, with 360 swivel and rotation and 16 inches of lift along the pole.

It sits below WALI and Suptek on reach and weight, but it is the one that names ultrawides, which matters because a 34 to 38 inch panel is wide and puts torque on the joint. It clamps on desks up to 3.25 inches thick by hand and ships with a grommet mount as well.

Buy it for a 34 inch ultrawide that weighs under 22 lb. Check the weight first, because many ultrawides run heavy and the listing does not give an extension figure, so confirm your desk depth before you commit.
cons: 22 lb cap rules out heavy panels
products.idealFor: 34 inch ultrawide owners with a monitor under 22 lb.
products.skipIf: Your ultrawide is a heavy gaming model.

products.name: Amazon Basics Single Monitor Stand
products.verdict: A steel arm with a 22 lb rating and the only stated warranty in the ranking.
products.description:
Amazon Basics sells a steel desk arm for 13 to 30 inch screens up to 22 lb with a detachable VESA plate for 75x75 and 100x100mm. Height adjusts from 7.9 to 14.2 inches, tilt runs from minus 15 to plus 85 degrees, and it clamps to desks 0.8 to 3.9 inches thick.

Its edge is the 1-year limited warranty, the only one stated in this group. The cost of that comfort is range: 14.2 inches of maximum height is the lowest here, and a 30 inch cap on screen size shuts out most ultrawides.

Buy it for a standard 24 to 27 inch monitor and a desk that is thick, since it accepts the widest edge. Taller sitters may find it cannot lift the screen to eye level, so check your seated eye height before ordering.
products.idealFor: Standard 24 to 27 inch monitors on thick desks.
products.skipIf: You sit tall or own an ultrawide.

products.name: HUANUO FlowLift Pro Monitor Arm
products.verdict: A spring arm with a tension window, but capped at 15.4 lb and 32 inches.
products.description:
The FlowLift Pro uses the maker's MechaSpring design, a tension indicator window and a snap-in quick-release VESA plate. It fits 13 to 32 inch screens weighing 4.4 to 15.4 lb on 75x75 or 100x100mm VESA, and is TÜV Rheinland certified at three times its load, per the listing.

It sits below the gas-spring HUANUO and VIVO on rating, because 15.4 lb is a tight ceiling. The tension window is the genuine innovation: you can see when the spring is set for your monitor, instead of guessing by feel. The maker also claims it resists pressure loss.

Buy it for a light 24 inch monitor where precision of setup matters. Mind the lower limit too: below 4.4 lb the arm will bounce, and the listing recommends wood desks only, so skip it for glass or irregular edges.
pros: One base, one screw to build
products.idealFor: Owners of lighter 24 to 27 inch monitors who adjust often.

products.name: HUANUO Gas Spring Single Monitor Arm
products.verdict: A gas-spring arm that lifts with one hand, but with a narrower tilt range.
products.description:
This HUANUO uses a gas-spring core for 13 to 32 inch screens weighing 4.4 to 19.8 lb on 75x75 or 100x100mm VESA. Tilt runs minus 50 to plus 30 degrees, swivel is plus or minus 90, and the screen lifts up to 39.6 cm.

It ranks below the FlowLift Pro on features but above it on capacity, since 19.8 lb is more than 15.4. Gas springs let you move the screen with one hand and hold it at any height, which is why people who swap between sitting and standing like them. The maker cites 20,000 motion tests.

It fits shoppers who want gas-spring feel on a lower budget. The plus 30 degree upper tilt is shorter than the sibling's, and the 4.4 lb minimum means very light screens will not stay put.
products.idealFor: Sit-stand users who reposition the monitor often.
products.skipIf: You need the widest tilt range.

products.name: ErGear Single Monitor Arm
products.verdict: The cheapest entry, with a clear 19.8 lb limit and tool-free setup.
products.description:
ErGear's arm fits 13 to 34 inch monitors up to 19.8 lb total, maxes at 100x100mm VESA, installs without tools and has a built-in cable channel. It is the lowest-priced arm here, in the under $25 bucket.

It ranks last because the listing details less: no reach figure, no height range and no warranty. Against WALI at 26.4 lb it gives up more than six pounds of headroom, and a 34 inch screen near that limit will sag sooner than on a sturdier arm.

Buy it for a 24 inch monitor that weighs well under 15 lb on a desk with simple clamp mounting. The VESA is limited to 100x100mm, so confirm your monitor's pattern before purchase.
products.idealFor: Light 24 inch monitors on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want long reach or a stated warranty.

whatMatters.detail: The rated load is a ceiling, not a target, and an arm run near its limit sags over months as the spring tires. WALI rates curved screens at 19.8 lb against 26.4 lb flat, because a curved panel hangs its weight further from the pole. Check your monitor's weight without the stand, and keep a margin below the figure.

VESA is the hole pattern on the back of the monitor, and the arm must match it. Every arm here fits 75x75 or 100x100mm, but ErGear stops at 100x100, and some thin or curved monitors need an adapter plate. Look up the pattern on your monitor's spec sheet before ordering, and confirm the arm's plate lists the same pattern.

Extension is how far the arm pulls the screen toward you, and height is how high it travels, and both decide whether the screen reaches eye level. Suptek offers 21.65 inches of extension, WALI 19.3, and Amazon Basics lifts only 7.9 to 14.2 inches. Compare those figures with your desk depth and seated eye line, especially if you are tall.

Clamps grip a limited edge range, and a crossbeam or lip under the top can block them. Amazon Basics takes 0.8 to 3.9 inches, Suptek up to 3.85 and WALI 0.39 to 2.76, while WALI and HUANUO advise wood tops with no crossbeam. Measure your desk edge in inches before shopping, and avoid glass or thin laminate without reinforcement.

Gas springs let you move a screen freely and hold any height, which helps for sit-stand use, and the HUANUO Gas Spring lifts up to 39.6 cm. The HUANUO FlowLift Pro uses a mechanical MechaSpring with a visible tension window instead. Either way, check the minimum weight, since both list a 4.4 lb floor below which the arm bounces.

howToChoose.intro: Match the screen first, then check weight.

cards.label: Gas spring
cards.text: One-handed movement, holds at any height. Picks: HUANUO Gas Spring, VIVO.

cards.label: Mechanical or fixed tilt
cards.text: Set once, stays put, with tension adjustments. Picks: HUANUO FlowLift Pro, Amazon Basics, WALI.

howToChoose.note: Pick gas spring if you reposition often, mechanical if you set it and forget it.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Enough reach to sit back from the screen, 20 lb or more of capacity, and cable guides to hide cords.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: WALI for most home offices, Suptek for big desks, Amazon Basics if you want a warranty.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You own a heavy ultrawide or switch screens often. The VIVO or WALI gives more headroom than the cheaper arms.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your monitor is light and fixed. ErGear or HUANUO FlowLift Pro will do.

faq.a: Check weight, screen size and VESA before anything else. WALI covers 13 to 34 inches at 26.4 lb flat, VIVO reaches ultrawides up to 38 inches at 22 lb, and ErGear tops out at 100x100mm VESA. If your screen fails any of the three, skip that arm.

Ignoring weight. A 27 lb monitor on a 22 lb VIVO or Amazon Basics arm will sag, and no tension setting can rescue an overloaded spring. Weigh your screen without its stand, then choose an arm like the WALI, which leaves headroom.

faq.q: Is an arm worth it over the stand?
faq.a: Yes, if you want desk space and eye-level alignment. The Suptek lifts 18.7 inches and extends 21.65, which lets you tuck a keyboard or notebook under the screen. A stand is cheaper but fixes the height and eats the desk surface.

Most arms clamp in minutes with a hex key. The HUANUO FlowLift Pro and ErGear install without tools on the VESA side, and Suptek has a tool-free clamp. Route cables through the channel and set tension last, with the monitor mounted.

Check clamp tightness every few months and re-tension after swapping monitors. The gas-spring HUANUO may creep down over time and need a retighten, and a wobble in the Suptek's long reach usually signals a loose clamp, not a bad arm.

Yes. WALI and HUANUO recommend wood tops with no crossbeam under the edge, so glass, thin laminate or desks with a lip need a different mount or a reinforcement plate. Amazon Basics accepts the thickest edge, up to 3.9 inches.

finalTake: WALI is the arm to buy if you want a high load rating and a reliable fit on a wood desk. Suptek wins on reach, VIVO on ultrawides, and Amazon Basics on warranty. Match your monitor's weight to the arm before anything else, and keep the load under about 80 percent of its limit.
